summary: One Flask service, shop, runs on EKS (two t3.large nodes) as one StatefulSet (stable pod names, service.instance.id = pod name, one node, warmed once so every pod's series exists before the runs) that KEDA 2.21.0 scales from 1 to 8 pods with the splunk-observability trigger, targetValue 10. Zero-code OpenTelemetry (0.66b2) pushes http.server.request.duration over OTLP to the Splunk OTel Collector agent (chart 0.163.1). Two configs differ only in the SignalFlow query (queries.json): total = each pod's orders counted over 20 s (delta rollup, sum over 20s, by k8s.pod.name), summed across pods, smoothed over 30 s, as orders a second; perpod = that same total divided by the pods that took orders in the last 20 s (.count() of the per-pod series, same stream). Same in every run: queryAggregator latest, duration 12, pollingInterval 5, useCachedMetrics, a 50 s scale-up window (up to 8 pods per 15 s) and a 300 s scale-down window. Each run starts shop at 3 pods (what the load needs, 30 / 10), so only the query decides whether it grows, applies the ScaledObject, records the HPA KEDA creates (target type and value), then sends 210 s of open-loop load at 30 orders a second and records the StatefulSet's replicas, the HPA's desired replicas and the metric value every 5 s. Runs: total-1, total-2 (reproduce.sh), perpod-1, perpod-2 (fix.sh). Measured per run: load_rps, hpa_target_value_type, replicas_max, replicas_final, seconds_to_settle, seconds_held_at_final, hpa_raw_recommendation_max, keda_scaler_errors, pods_running_end, ready_replicas_end, metric_value_end, hpa_desired_max, seconds_to_max, splunk_pods_reporting (fix.sh fails a per-pod run if it differs from ready_replicas_end); fix.sh also reads each run's total, per-pod rate and reporting pods back from Splunk.
expected: reproduce.sh: in total-1 and total-2 the HPA keda-hpa-shop has an external metric target of type Value and the Deployment reaches the maximum of 8 pods under a fixed 30 orders a second, then HERO_RESULT: reproduced. fix.sh: in perpod-1 and perpod-2 the HPA target is also type Value, the Deployment never goes past 4 pods, ends at 3 (load over target, 30 / 10) or 4 within the HPA's 10% tolerance, and holds that count for at least the last 60 s of the load, then HERO_RESULT: fixed. load_rps, seconds_to_settle, hpa_raw_recommendation_max, keda_scaler_errors and splunk_pods_reporting are measured results, not conditions.

# Scale on Splunk metrics with KEDA: the total request rate versus the rate per pod

One small Python service, `shop`, runs on EKS (two t3.large nodes) as one StatefulSet (on one node) that KEDA 2.21.0 scales from 1 to
at most 8 pods. Zero-code OpenTelemetry (`opentelemetry-instrument`, 0.66b2) records `http.server.request.duration` for
every order and pushes it over OTLP to the Splunk OTel Collector agent on the pod's node (chart 0.163.1), which sends it
to Splunk Observability Cloud. KEDA's `splunk-observability` trigger runs a SignalFlow query of that metric and scales
toward a target of 10 requests a second.

Only the query's last step differs between the two configs (both in `queries.json`). Both first count each pod's orders over the
last 20 s (`rollup='delta'`, then `.sum(over='20s')`; a removed pod drops out once
its last point leaves the window) into one series per pod with
`.sum(by=['k8s.pod.name'])` (the app sets `k8s.pod.name` on its resource); `.scale(0.05)` makes that orders a second.

total (total-1, total-2, `reproduce.sh`) then adds the pods up: orders a second across all pods. perpod (perpod-1,
perpod-2, `fix.sh`) divides that same total by the pods that took orders in the last 20 s (`.count()` of the per-pod series, from the same
stream): orders a second per pod.

The two queries exactly as `queries.json` holds them (RUN becomes the lab's label, `start_run` prints the filled query
and saves it as `query-<run>.txt`):

```text
total:  data('http.server.request.duration_count', filter=filter('service.name', 'shop') and filter('run', 'RUN') and filter('http.request.method', 'POST') and filter('http.response.status_code', '200'), rollup='delta').sum(over='20s').sum(by=['k8s.pod.name']).sum().mean(over='30s').scale(0.05).publish()
perpod: (data('http.server.request.duration_count', filter=filter('service.name', 'shop') and filter('run', 'RUN') and filter('http.request.method', 'POST') and filter('http.response.status_code', '200'), rollup='delta').sum(over='20s').sum(by=['k8s.pod.name']).sum().mean(over='30s').scale(0.05) / data('http.server.request.duration_count', filter=filter('service.name', 'shop') and filter('run', 'RUN') and filter('http.request.method', 'POST') and filter('http.response.status_code', '200'), rollup='delta').sum(over='20s').sum(by=['k8s.pod.name']).count()).publish()
```

The metric name is the one Splunk stores: the Collector agent's signalfx exporter turns the OTLP histogram
`http.server.request.duration` into `http.server.request.duration_count` (plus `_sum` and `_bucket`), the same name lab 226
read back with this chart version. The trigger in `k8s/30-scale.yaml`, with QUERY replaced by one of the two:

```yaml
- type: splunk-observability
  useCachedMetrics: true
  metadata: { query: "QUERY", duration: "12", targetValue: "10", activationTargetValue: "1", queryAggregator: "latest" }
  authenticationRef: { name: splunk-keda }
```

Why this shape: the rehearsals showed KEDA's 12 s live stream can end on a point that holds only some pods, and a
stream at 1 s resolution read a 10 s rate point as 300. A 20 s order count per pod does not depend on the resolution,
and `.mean(over='30s')` blends three points, so one partial read can't drive scaling. The load is fixed, so the total holds
steady while pods are added, and a new pod counts as soon as its first points arrive, so total ÷ pods tracks the rate
per pod quickly. Earlier versions lagged by up to a minute (a smoothed mean of per-pod series), or got no data in
KEDA's 12 s live stream for a whole run (dividing by `k8s.statefulset.ready_pods`, a second source). If a query named a metric with no data, KEDA would log "query returned no data points" (counted in `keda_scaler_errors`)
and the HPA would stay at 1 pod, so the total runs would fail `reproduce.sh` rather than pass for the wrong reason.

Everything else is the same in every run (`k8s/30-scale.yaml`): `targetValue: "10"`, `queryAggregator: latest`,
`duration: "12"`, `pollingInterval: 5`, `useCachedMetrics: true`, 1 to 8 pods, and the same HPA behaviour: a 50 s
scale-up stabilization window with a policy of up to 8 pods per 15 s (so one step can go from 3 to 8), and a 300 s
scale-down window. The Kubernetes default scale-up window is 0 s. The 50 s window is part of this recipe in both configs:
it filters out a single odd read from KEDA's live stream. With a fixed 210 s load, a longer window would not leave the
total runs time to climb, because new pods take a while to appear in the live query (the timelines show how long). `hpa_raw_recommendation_max` records what the HPA's formula asked for with no window.

Why a StatefulSet: Splunk keys a series on its dimensions, and the Python SDK sets a random `service.instance.id` per
process, so every new pod used to start brand-new series, which KEDA's live query picked up only after a delay (up to
minutes in the rehearsals). Here pods are `shop-0` to `shop-7` with `service.instance.id` set to the pod name, all on node
A, so a pod keeps the same series every time it starts. `reproduce.sh` warms all 8 once (20 s of load) and waits until
Splunk holds all 8 pods' series. Each run starts at 3 pods (`shop-0` to `shop-2`), the count the load needs (30 / 10), so only the query decides
whether more are added. An earlier run that started at 1 pod overshot with the per-pod query too, because new pods appear
in KEDA's live read 30–45 s late; every run shares the label `<lab>-shop` and is told
apart by its load window, and each run numbers its orders in its own block so every pod counts that run's orders. Each run then applies the ScaledObject, records the HPA KEDA creates
and sends 210 s of load at 30 orders a second, a new connection per order (load over target: 30 / 10 = 3 pods).

What is measured, per run:
- `load_rps`: orders that succeeded a second, counted by the load (each pod's own count is printed beside it).
- `hpa_target_value_type`: 1 when the HPA `keda-hpa-shop` has an external metric target of type `Value` (the type and
  value are printed, and the whole HPA is saved to `hpa-<run>.json`).
- `replicas_max`: the most replicas the StatefulSet had during the load, read every 5 s.
- `replicas_final`: the StatefulSet's replicas when the load ended.
- `seconds_to_settle`: seconds from the load's start to the last change in the StatefulSet's replicas.
- `seconds_held_at_final`: seconds the Deployment held its final replica count before the load ended.
- `hpa_raw_recommendation_max`: the largest `ceil(replicas x value / target)` across the 5 s samples, what the HPA's
  formula asks for before the stabilization window.
- `keda_scaler_errors`: warning events on this run's ScaledObject (for example a query window with no data point).
- `pods_running_end`: shop pods that took orders in this run.
- `splunk_pods_reporting`: pods with a request-rate series in Splunk at the end of the load (`.count()` of the per-pod
  series). Every ready pod should report, so `fix.sh` fails a per-pod run when this
  differs from `ready_replicas_end`.
- `ready_replicas_end`: the StatefulSet's ready replicas at the end of the load.
- `metric_value_end`: the last metric value the HPA read from KEDA (requests a second).
- `hpa_desired_max`, `seconds_to_max`: the HPA's highest desired replicas, and the first sample at the maximum of 8 pods
  (-1 if never), so a total run that stops short can be diagnosed without a rerun.
- Each run's effective ScaledObject is saved as `scaledobject-<run>.yaml` next to `hpa-<run>.json`.

Every 5 s the StatefulSet's desired and ready replicas, the HPA's desired replicas and the metric value it read go to
`timeline-<run>.txt`, and each change is printed. After the runs, `fix.sh` reads every run back from Splunk with the same
metric: the total rate, the rate per pod and how many pods reported, at the end of the load.

`reproduce.sh` prints `HERO_RESULT: reproduced` when both total runs have a `Value` target and reach the maximum of 8 pods.
`fix.sh` prints `HERO_RESULT: fixed` when both per-pod runs never go past 4 pods, end at 3 (load over target) or 4 if the
HPA's 10% tolerance lands there, and hold that count for at least the last 60 s of the load.

## Why the two queries behave differently

For an external metric with a `Value` target, the HPA computes `desired = ceil(current replicas x value / target)`.
With the total, a fixed load keeps the value at about 30 however many pods run, so every step asks for about 3 times the
pods it has, up to the maximum. Divided by ready pods, the value falls as pods share the load (30 over 3 pods is 10), so the
ratio reaches 1 and the replica count stays at load over target.

## Run it in your own account

You need an AWS account, Terraform, kubectl, helm and jq, and a Splunk Observability Cloud org with an ingest token (for
the Collector) and an API token (for KEDA's SignalFlow queries and the lab's reads).

```bash
export AWS_REGION=eu-central-1 LAB_NAME=keda-lab TF_VAR_lab_name=keda-lab
export SPLUNK_REALM=us1 SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN=your-ingest-token SPLUNK_API_TOKEN=your-api-token
terraform init && terraform apply -auto-approve   # EKS 1.34, two t3.large nodes
./reproduce.sh     # the Collector agent, KEDA 2.21.0 and shop; total-1 and total-2
./fix.sh           # perpod-1 and perpod-2, then all four runs read back from Splunk
./cleanup.sh && terraform destroy -auto-approve
```

The pipeline's runner adds the S3 backend, the default AWS provider and the `region`, `lab_name` and
`permissions_boundary` variables; in your own copy, declare those three variables and the provider. The cluster costs
money while it runs. Each script fits in 14 minutes, so each run's load is 210 s.

## What this lab does not test

- Other load levels, targets or pod ranges; one workload with one route.
- `metricType: AverageValue` on the trigger: KEDA 2.21.0's scaler builds the HPA target as `Value` in code
  (`GetMetricSpecForScaling`), which `hpa_target_value_type` checks in every run.
- Scale-down: each run ends while the load is still on, and the next run starts from 1 pod.
- The per-pod query with the default 0 s scale-up window; `hpa_raw_recommendation_max` shows what the formula asked for.

## Background and sources

- KEDA 2.21 docs, Splunk Observability scaler (keda.sh/docs/2.21/scalers/splunk-observability): the trigger's `query`,
  `duration`, `targetValue`, `activationTargetValue` and `queryAggregator` (`min`, `max`, `avg`, `sum`, `count` or
  `latest`), and the TriggerAuthentication's `accessToken` and `realm`.
- KEDA v2.21.0 source, `pkg/scalers/splunk_observability_scaler.go`: `GetMetricSpecForScaling` sets the target with
  `GetMetricTargetMili(v2.ValueMetricType, targetValue)`, so the HPA target is `Value`; a query window with no data points
  returns the error "query returned no data points".
- kedacore/keda issue 8297: the splunk-observability scaler builds the HPA target as `Value` and doesn't read the
  trigger's `metricType`, so with a metric that doesn't fall as pods are added, the HPA keeps adding replicas up to
  `maxReplicaCount`.
- Kubernetes docs, Horizontal Pod Autoscaling, algorithm details: `desiredReplicas = ceil[currentReplicas *
  (currentMetricValue / desiredMetricValue)]`, a default tolerance of 10%, and scale-up and scale-down stabilization
  windows set with `behavior`.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The free check, on a GitHub runner with Docker, before AWS is paid for. It runs the lab's real code (the files the
# manifests carry): the shop app with the pinned packages and zero-code OpenTelemetry, the real load, and a Collector
# (contrib 0.165.0) whose exporter writes to a file instead of Splunk.
# It proves, before AWS: the app takes every order; OpenTelemetry records each POST once in http.server.request.duration
# with service.name shop, the run label and http.response.status_code 200 (the series KEDA's query reads); both queries in
# queries.json fill into the ScaledObject as one valid line; and the two queries differ only in sum versus mean.
# Scaling needs Kubernetes, KEDA and Splunk, so the rehearsal and the paid lab test that.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
mkdir -p c/app c/load c/conf c/out c/venv
chmod 777 c/out

python3 - <<'PY'
import json, re
def block(path, key):
    text = open(path).read()
    m = re.search(rf"^  {re.escape(key)}: \|\n((?:    .*\n|\n)+)", text, re.M)
    return "\n".join(line[4:] for line in m[1].splitlines()) + "\n"
for k in ("requirements.txt", "shop.py"):
    open(f"c/app/{k}", "w").write(block("k8s/00-build.yaml", k))
open("c/load/load.py", "w").write(block("k8s/20-load.yaml", "load.py"))
q = json.load(open("queries.json"))
scale = open("k8s/30-scale.yaml").read()
assert scale.count('"QUERY"') == 1, "the ScaledObject needs exactly one QUERY placeholder"
for k in ("total", "perpod"):
    v = q[k].replace("RUN", "lab-check-1").replace("CLUSTER", "lab-check")
    assert '"' not in v and "&" not in v and "\n" not in v, f"{k}: the query can't carry a double quote, & or newline"
    assert v.count("lab-check-1") == (2 if k == "perpod" else 1) and "filter('service.name', 'shop')" in v and "rollup='delta'" in v, k
    assert ".sum(over='20s').sum(by=['k8s.pod.name'])." in v, f"{k}: one 20 s order count per pod first"
    filled = scale.replace('"QUERY"', '"' + v + '"')
    assert f'query: "{v}"' in filled
    print(f"{k}: {v}")
tot = q["total"][:-len(".publish()")]
assert q["perpod"] == "(" + tot + " / " + tot[:tot.index(".sum().mean(over='30s')")] + ".count()).publish()", "perpod must be the total divided by the count of per-pod series"
print("queries: fill into the ScaledObject; perpod is the total divided by the pods reporting")
PY
IMAGE=$(grep -m1 -oE 'python:[^ "]+' k8s/10-app.yaml)
COLLECTOR=otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib:0.165.0
cat > c/conf/col.yaml <<YAML
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      http:
        endpoint: 0.0.0.0:4318
exporters:
  file:
    path: /out/col.json
service:
  pipelines:
    metrics:
      receivers: [otlp]
      exporters: [file]
YAML
docker network create lab >/dev/null

echo "== One virtualenv with the pinned packages, as the build Jobs make it"
docker run --rm -v "$PWD/c/app:/app:ro" -v "$PWD/c/venv:/lab/venv" "$IMAGE" sh -c '
  python -m venv /lab/venv && /lab/venv/bin/pip install -q --no-cache-dir -r /app/requirements.txt &&
  /lab/venv/bin/pip freeze | grep -iE "^(flask|waitress|opentelemetry-(distro|sdk|instrumentation-flask))=="'
docker pull -q "$COLLECTOR" >/dev/null
docker run -d --name col --network lab -v "$PWD/c/conf:/conf:ro" -v "$PWD/c/out:/out" "$COLLECTOR" "--config=/conf/col.yaml" >/dev/null
RUN=check-1
for p in shop-a shop-b; do
  docker run -d --name "$p" --network lab -v "$PWD/c/app:/lab/app:ro" -v "$PWD/c/venv:/lab/venv:ro" \
    -e POD_NAME="$p" -e LAB_RUN="$RUN" -e OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=shop -e OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://col:4318 \
    -e OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=http/protobuf -e "OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES=deployment.environment=check,k8s.pod.name=$p,run=$RUN" \
    -e OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER=none -e OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER=otlp -e OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL=10000 -e OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER=none \
    -e OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN=http -e OTEL_PYTHON_FLASK_EXCLUDED_URLS=stats,healthz -e PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
    "$IMAGE" /lab/venv/bin/opentelemetry-instrument /lab/venv/bin/python /lab/app/shop.py >/dev/null
done
for p in shop-a shop-b; do
  for i in $(seq 1 60); do docker exec "$p" /lab/venv/bin/python -c "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://localhost:8080/healthz', timeout=2)" 2>/dev/null && break; sleep 1; done
done
echo "== The load: 20 s at 30 orders a second to shop-a and 20 s at 10 a second to shop-b"
docker run -d --name load-a --network lab -v "$PWD/c/load:/load:ro" -e RATE=30 -e LOAD_SECONDS=20 -e RUN=$RUN -e FIRST=1 -e SHOP_HOST=shop-a "$IMAGE" python /load/load.py >/dev/null
docker run --rm --network lab -v "$PWD/c/load:/load:ro" -e RATE=10 -e LOAD_SECONDS=20 -e RUN=$RUN -e FIRST=1001 -e SHOP_HOST=shop-b "$IMAGE" python /load/load.py > c/load-b.txt
docker wait load-a >/dev/null; docker logs load-a > c/load-a.txt
sleep 22
for p in shop-a shop-b; do
  docker exec "$p" /lab/venv/bin/python -c 'import json, urllib.request
d = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen("http://localhost:8080/stats", timeout=5)); print(d["pod"], d["run"], d["orders"])' | tee -a c/pods.txt
done
docker rm -f shop-a shop-b load-a >/dev/null; sleep 3; docker rm -f col >/dev/null

python3 - "$RUN" <<'PY'
import json, re, sys
run = sys.argv[1]
fail = lambda m: (print(f"CHECK FAILED: {m}"), sys.exit(1))
oks = {x: int(re.search(r"ok=(\d+)", open(f"c/load-{x}.txt").read())[1]) for x in "ab"}
pods = {l.split()[0]: int(l.split()[2]) for l in open("c/pods.txt")}
print(f"orders ok {oks}; the pods took {pods}")
pods.get("shop-a") == oks["a"] and pods.get("shop-b") == oks["b"] or fail("a pod didn't take every order sent to it")
last = {}
for line in open("c/out/col.json"):
    for rm in json.loads(line).get("resourceMetrics", []):
        res = {a["key"]: list(a["value"].values())[0] for a in rm["resource"].get("attributes", [])}
        for sm in rm.get("scopeMetrics", []):
            for m in sm.get("metrics", []):
                if m["name"] != "http.server.request.duration":
                    continue
                for dp in m.get("histogram", {}).get("dataPoints", []):
                    attrs = {a["key"]: list(a["value"].values())[0] for a in dp.get("attributes", [])}
                    key = (res.get("service.name"), res.get("run"), res.get("k8s.pod.name"), attrs.get("http.request.method"),
                           str(attrs.get("http.response.status_code")))
                    t = int(dp.get("timeUnixNano", 0))
                    if m["histogram"].get("aggregationTemporality") == 1:     # delta: each point counts since the last one
                        last[key] = (t, last.get(key, (0, 0))[1] + int(dp.get("count", 0)))
                    elif t >= last.get(key, (0, 0))[0]:
                        last[key] = (t, int(dp.get("count", 0)))
print("series:", {k: v[1] for k, v in last.items()})
all(k[2] for k in last if k[0] == "shop") or fail("a shop series has no k8s.pod.name, so the queries can't group by pod")
per = {k[2]: v[1] for k, v in last.items() if k[0] == "shop" and k[1] == run and k[3] == "POST" and k[4] == "200"}
per.get("shop-a") == oks["a"] and per.get("shop-b") == oks["b"] or fail(f"OpenTelemetry's POST 200 count per pod {per} doesn't match the orders {oks}")
total = sum(per.values()); mean = total / len(per)
print(f"OpenTelemetry POST 200 per pod {per}: total {total}, mean {mean:.0f} (the sum and the mean KEDA's two queries take, as counts)")
temps = {m["histogram"].get("aggregationTemporality") for line in open("c/out/col.json") for rm in json.loads(line).get("resourceMetrics", [])
         for sm in rm.get("scopeMetrics", []) for m in sm.get("metrics", []) if m["name"] == "http.server.request.duration"}
temps == {2} or fail(f"http.server.request.duration temporality {temps}, expected cumulative (2)")
print("temporality: cumulative")
print("CHECK PASSED")
PY

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Never fail hard. Nothing here creates AWS resources outside Terraform (no LoadBalancers, Ingresses or volumes).
set +e
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
name=$(terraform output -raw cluster_name 2>/dev/null)
if [ -n "$name" ]; then
  aws eks update-kubeconfig --name "$name" --region "$AWS_REGION" >/dev/null 2>&1
  if kubectl --request-timeout=15s get nodes >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    timeout 60 kubectl -n demo delete scaledobject shop --ignore-not-found >/dev/null 2>&1
    timeout 180 helm uninstall keda -n keda --timeout 120s >/dev/null 2>&1
    timeout 180 helm uninstall splunk-otel-collector -n splunk --timeout 120s >/dev/null 2>&1
    timeout 120 kubectl delete namespace demo keda splunk --wait=false >/dev/null 2>&1
    echo "cleanup: ScaledObject deleted, helm releases uninstalled, namespaces deleting"
  else
    echo "cleanup: cluster not reachable, nothing to remove"
  fi
else
  echo "cleanup: no cluster output, nothing to remove"
fi
exit 0

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# BUILD: the same KEDA ScaledObject with one change in its SignalFlow query: the total divided by the pods that took orders
# in the last 20 s (.count() of the per-pod series, from the same stream). Starting from the 3 pods the load needs, the rate per pod is at the target, so the HPA has no reason to add pods. Runs
# perpod-1 and perpod-2 with the same load, target, pod range and HPA behaviour as total-1 and total-2, then reads all
# four runs back from Splunk.
set -uo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
. ./lib.sh
. ./splunk.sh

start_clock 830 not_fixed

aws eks update-kubeconfig --name "$(terraform output -raw cluster_name)" --region "$AWS_REGION" >/dev/null || fail "could not write kubeconfig"
for v in SPLUNK_REALM SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN SPLUNK_API_TOKEN; do [ -n "${!v:-}" ] || fail "$v is not set"; done
NODE_A=$(cat node-a.txt) || fail "no node recorded"
[ -s result-total-1.txt ] && [ -s result-total-2.txt ] || fail "reproduce.sh's runs are missing"

echo "== 1. The one change: the query's last step"
diff <(jq -r .total queries.json | tr '.' '\n') <(jq -r .perpod queries.json | tr '.' '\n') | grep '^[<>]' | sed 's/^/  /'

for run in perpod-1 perpod-2; do
  echo "== Run $run: KEDA on the request rate per pod (the total divided by the pods taking orders), target $TARGET a second, $MAX_PODS pods at most"
  start_run "$run" 90
  [ "$HPA_TYPE" = Value ] && v1=1 || v1=0
  load_run "$run"
  echo "$REPLICAS_MAX $REPLICAS_FINAL $SETTLE $v1 $HELD $READY_END" > "result-$run.txt"
done
kubectl -n demo delete scaledobject shop --ignore-not-found --wait=false >/dev/null 2>&1

echo "== 2. All four runs in Splunk"
for run in total-1 total-2 perpod-1 perpod-2; do
  splunk_run "$run"
  echo "${SP_PODS:-0}" > "splunk-pods-$run.txt"
done

echo "== 3. Side by side"
printf '  %-9s %-8s %-10s %-12s %-12s %-10s\n' run "HPA type" "most pods" "pods at end" "last change" "held for"
for run in total-1 total-2 perpod-1 perpod-2; do
  read -r mx fin st v held rdy < "result-$run.txt"
  printf '  %-9s %-8s %-10s %-12s %-12s %-10s\n' "$run" "$([ "$v" = 1 ] && echo Value || echo other)" "$mx" "$fin" "${st}s" "${held}s"
done

# Fixed: with the per-pod query, both runs never went past 4 pods (no overshoot), ended at load over target (30 / 10 = 3,
# or 4 if the HPA's 10% tolerance lands there) and held that count for at least the last 60 s of the load.
for run in perpod-1 perpod-2; do
  read -r mx fin st v held rdy < "result-$run.txt"
  sp=$(cat "splunk-pods-$run.txt")
  [ "$sp" = "$rdy" ] || fail "$run: $sp pods reporting to Splunk but $rdy ready, so the mean isn't the rate per pod"
  [ "$mx" -le 4 ] || fail "$run went up to $mx pods, past load over target"
  [ "$fin" -ge 3 ] && [ "$fin" -le 4 ] || fail "$run ended at $fin pods, not at load over target (3)"
  [ "${held:-0}" -ge 60 ] || fail "$run held $fin pods for only ${held:-0}s at the end, so it hadn't settled"
done
emit fixed

apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: app-src
  namespace: demo
data:
  requirements.txt: |
    flask==3.1.3
    waitress==3.0.2
    opentelemetry-distro==0.66b2
    opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http==1.45.2
    opentelemetry-instrumentation-flask==0.66b2

  shop.py: |
    # shop: takes orders. Zero-code OpenTelemetry records http.server.request.duration for every request and pushes it
    # over OTLP to the Splunk OTel Collector agent on the pod's node, so Splunk sees each pod's request rate.
    # GET /stats says how many orders this pod took, so the lab knows the truth without Splunk.
    import os, threading
    from flask import Flask
    from waitress import serve

    RUN, POD = os.environ.get("LAB_RUN", "none"), os.environ.get("POD_NAME", "local")
    app = Flask(__name__)
    taken, blocks, lock = [0], {}, threading.Lock()


    @app.post("/orders/<int:order>")
    def create(order):
        with lock:
            taken[0] += 1
            blocks[order // 100000] = blocks.get(order // 100000, 0) + 1   # each run numbers its orders in its own block
        return {"order": order, "ok": True}


    @app.get("/stats")
    def stats():
        with lock:
            return {"pod": POD, "run": RUN, "orders": taken[0], "blocks": blocks}


    @app.get("/healthz")
    def healthz():
        return "ok"


    if __name__ == "__main__":
        print(f"SHOP pod={POD} run={RUN} threads=16", flush=True)
        serve(app, host="0.0.0.0", port=8080, threads=16)

apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: load
  namespace: demo
data:
  load.py: |
    # Open-loop load: RATE orders a second for LOAD_SECONDS to the shop Service, a new connection per order, so the
    # Service spreads them over every ready pod. Every order is counted here, so the lab knows the true rate.
    import os, threading, time, http.client
    RATE, SECONDS = int(os.environ.get("RATE", "30")), int(os.environ.get("LOAD_SECONDS", "210"))
    HOST, PORT, RUN, FIRST = os.environ.get("SHOP_HOST", "shop"), 8080, os.environ.get("RUN", "run"), int(os.environ.get("FIRST", "1"))
    ok, failed, lock = [0], [0], threading.Lock()

    def one(n):
        good = False
        try:
            c = http.client.HTTPConnection(HOST, PORT, timeout=5)
            c.request("POST", f"/orders/{n}")
            good = c.getresponse().status == 200
            c.close()
        except Exception:
            pass
        with lock:
            (ok if good else failed)[0] += 1

    t0, n = time.time(), FIRST
    print(f"LOAD start={t0:.0f} run={RUN} rate={RATE} seconds={SECONDS}", flush=True)
    for sec in range(SECONDS):
        for i in range(RATE):
            threading.Thread(target=one, args=(n,), daemon=True).start(); n += 1
            time.sleep(max(0, t0 + sec + (i + 1) / RATE - time.time()))
    time.sleep(6)
    print(f"LOAD end={time.time():.0f} sent={n - FIRST} ok={ok[0]} failed={failed[0]}", flush=True)

# KEDA scales shop on a SignalFlow query of this run's request rate in Splunk Observability Cloud. Only QUERY differs
# between the two configs (total.query and perpod.query). Everything else is the same in every run: the target of
# 10 requests a second, 1 to 8 pods, and the same HPA behaviour (a 50 s scale-up window, so a new pod's traffic reaches
# Splunk before the next step). The TriggerAuthentication reads the realm and API token from the splunk-keda Secret,
# which reproduce.sh creates from the environment.
apiVersion: keda.sh/v1alpha1
kind: TriggerAuthentication
metadata:
  name: splunk-keda
  namespace: demo
spec:
  secretTargetRef:
    - { parameter: accessToken, name: splunk-keda, key: accessToken }
    - { parameter: realm, name: splunk-keda, key: realm }

kind: ScaledObject

  namespace: demo
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: StatefulSet
    name: shop
  pollingInterval: 5
  cooldownPeriod: 300
  minReplicaCount: 1
  maxReplicaCount: 8
  advanced:

      behavior:
        scaleUp:
          stabilizationWindowSeconds: 50
          policies:
            - { type: Pods, value: 8, periodSeconds: 15 }
        scaleDown:
          stabilizationWindowSeconds: 300
  triggers:
    - type: splunk-observability
      useCachedMetrics: true
      metadata:
        query: "QUERY"
        duration: "12"
        targetValue: "10"
        activationTargetValue: "1"
        queryAggregator: "latest"
      authenticationRef:
        name: splunk-keda

# Shared by reproduce.sh and fix.sh. Sourced, never run alone. A run = one KEDA query (total or perpod, queries.json), the
# shop StatefulSet reset to 3 pods (same pods, series and label every run), then 210 s of open-loop load at 30 orders a second while the
# replicas, the HPA's target and the metric it reads are recorded every 5 s. Only the query differs between configs.
export LC_ALL=C
LOAD_SECONDS=210
TARGET=10
MAX_PODS=8
START_PODS=3   # every run starts at the pods the load needs (30 / 10), so only the query decides whether it grows
. ./helpers.sh

# Reset: no ScaledObject (so no HPA) and shop back to shop-0..shop-2, whose series Splunk already holds. Then the
# ScaledObject with this run's query. KEDA creates the HPA keda-hpa-shop, whose target type and value are recorded.
start_run() {   # run label, seconds allowed
  local q t0 tt
  kubectl -n demo delete scaledobject shop --ignore-not-found --wait=true --timeout=60s >/dev/null 2>&1
  t0=$(date +%s)
  while kubectl -n demo get hpa keda-hpa-shop >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ $(( $(date +%s) - t0 )) -lt 60 ]; do sleep 3; done
  kubectl -n demo scale statefulset/shop --replicas="$START_PODS" >/dev/null || fail "could not scale shop to $START_PODS"
  kubectl -n demo rollout status statefulset/shop --timeout="$(cap "$2" 300)s" >/dev/null || { why; fail "shop did not roll out for $1"; }
  t0=$(date +%s)
  while [ "$(kubectl -n demo get pods -l app=shop --no-headers 2>/dev/null | grep -c ' Running')" != "$START_PODS" ] && [ $(( $(date +%s) - t0 )) -lt 90 ]; do sleep 3; done
  kubectl -n demo wait statefulset/shop --for=jsonpath='{.status.readyReplicas}'="$START_PODS" --timeout=60s >/dev/null || { why; fail "shop is not at $START_PODS ready pods before $1"; }
  [ "$(kubectl -n demo get pods -l app=shop --no-headers 2>/dev/null | wc -l)" = "$START_PODS" ] || { why; fail "not $START_PODS shop pods before $1"; }
  q=$(query_for "$1")
  echo "$q" > "query-$1.txt"
  [ "$q" = "$(jq -r --arg k "${1%-*}" '.[$k]' queries.json | sed -e "s/RUN/$LAB_NAME-shop/g" -e "s/CLUSTER/$LAB_NAME/g")" ] || fail "$1: applied query differs from queries.json"
  echo "$1 query: $q"
  local y; y=$(cat k8s/30-scale.yaml)          # the query has no & or double quote, so a plain replacement is safe
  printf '%s\n' "${y//\"QUERY\"/\"$q\"}" | kubectl apply -f - >/dev/null || fail "could not apply the ScaledObject for $1"
  t0=$(date +%s); tt=""
  while [ $(( $(date +%s) - t0 )) -lt "$(cap 90 300)" ]; do
    tt=$(kubectl -n demo get hpa keda-hpa-shop -o jsonpath='{.spec.metrics[0].external.target.type} {.spec.metrics[0].external.target.value} {.spec.minReplicas}-{.spec.maxReplicas}' 2>/dev/null)
    [ -n "${tt%% *}" ] && break
    sleep 3
  done
  [ -n "${tt%% *}" ] || { kubectl -n demo describe scaledobject shop | tail -15; fail "KEDA created no HPA for $1"; }
  kubectl -n demo get hpa keda-hpa-shop -o json > "hpa-$1.json"
  kubectl -n demo get scaledobject shop -o yaml > "scaledobject-$1.yaml"
  check_hpa "$1"   # helpers.sh: live HPA has the 50 s window, 1-8 pods
  SO_UID=$(kubectl -n demo get scaledobject shop -o jsonpath='{.metadata.uid}')   # this run's events only
  echo "$1 HPA keda-hpa-shop: external metric target type ${tt%% *}, value $(echo "$tt" | cut -d' ' -f2), replicas $(echo "$tt" | cut -d' ' -f3)"
  HPA_TYPE=${tt%% *}
  echo "HERO_MEASURE: hpa_target_value_type[$1]=$([ "$HPA_TYPE" = Value ] && echo 1 || echo 0)"
}

# The load, and every 5 s: the StatefulSet's desired and ready replicas, the HPA's desired replicas and the metric value
# it read (KEDA's latest value from the query). The whole timeline goes to timeline-<run>.txt; changes are printed.
load_run() {   # run label
  local t0 now el spec ready want cur line last="" lastspec=$START_PODS changed=0 maxr=$START_PODS st ok sent failed rps v rec raw=1 held errs tomax=-1 dmax=0 vend=0
  kubectl -n demo delete pod load --ignore-not-found --wait=true >/dev/null 2>&1
  sed -e "s/NODE_A/$NODE_A/" -e "s/value: \"RUN\"/value: \"$1\"/" -e "s/value: \"FIRST\"/value: \"$(first_order "$1")\"/" \
      -e "s/value: \"LOAD_SECONDS\"/value: \"$LOAD_SECONDS\"/" k8s/20-load.yaml | kubectl apply -f - >/dev/null || fail "could not start the load"
  kubectl -n demo wait pod/load --for=jsonpath='{.status.phase}'=Running --timeout=60s >/dev/null || { why; fail "the load pod did not start"; }
  t0=$(date +%s)
  echo "t(s) deployment_replicas ready hpa_desired metric_value raw_recommendation" > "timeline-$1.txt"
  for i in $(seq 1 60); do
    now=$(date +%s); el=$(( now - t0 ))
    spec=$(kubectl -n demo get statefulset shop -o jsonpath='{.spec.replicas}' 2>/dev/null)
    ready=$(kubectl -n demo get statefulset shop -o jsonpath='{.status.readyReplicas}' 2>/dev/null)
    want=$(kubectl -n demo get hpa keda-hpa-shop -o jsonpath='{.status.desiredReplicas}' 2>/dev/null)
    cur=$(kubectl -n demo get hpa keda-hpa-shop -o jsonpath='{.status.currentMetrics[0].external.current.value}' 2>/dev/null)
    # What the HPA's formula asks for from this sample with no stabilization window: ceil(replicas x value / target).
    # The value comes as a Kubernetes quantity (30 or 29500m).
    rec=-
    if [ -n "$cur" ] && [ -n "$spec" ]; then
      case "$cur" in *m) v=$(awk -v x="${cur%m}" 'BEGIN {printf "%.3f", x / 1000}') ;; *) v=$cur ;; esac
      rec=$(awk -v r="$spec" -v v="$v" -v t="$TARGET" 'BEGIN {x = r * v / t; c = int(x); if (c < x) c++; if (c < 1) c = 1; print c}')
      [ "$rec" -gt "$raw" ] && raw=$rec
    fi
    line="${spec:-?} ${ready:-0} ${want:-?} ${cur:-none}"
    echo "$el $line $rec" >> "timeline-$1.txt"
    [ "$line" != "$last" ] && echo "  $1 t=${el}s: deployment ${spec:-?} (ready ${ready:-0}), HPA wants ${want:-?}, metric ${cur:-none}"
    last=$line
    if [ -n "$spec" ] && [ "$spec" != "$lastspec" ]; then changed=$el; lastspec=$spec; fi
    [ -n "$spec" ] && [ "$spec" -gt "$maxr" ] && maxr=$spec
    [ "$tomax" = -1 ] && [ "${spec:-0}" = "$MAX_PODS" ] && tomax=$el
    [ -n "$want" ] && [ "$want" -gt "$dmax" ] && dmax=$want
    [ -n "$cur" ] && vend=${v:-0}
    st=$(kubectl -n demo get pod load -o jsonpath='{.status.phase}' 2>/dev/null)
    [ "$st" = Succeeded ] || [ "$st" = Failed ] && break
    [ "$el" -ge $(( LOAD_SECONDS + 15 )) ] && break
    sleep 5
  done
  kubectl -n demo wait pod/load --for=jsonpath='{.status.phase}'=Succeeded --timeout=30s >/dev/null || { kubectl -n demo logs load --tail=5; fail "the load did not finish in $1"; }
  kubectl -n demo logs load > "load-$1.txt"
  ok=$(sed -n 's/^LOAD end=.* ok=\([0-9]*\).*/\1/p' "load-$1.txt"); sent=$(sed -n 's/^LOAD end=.* sent=\([0-9]*\).*/\1/p' "load-$1.txt")
  failed=$(sed -n 's/^LOAD end=.* failed=\([0-9]*\).*/\1/p' "load-$1.txt")
  held=$(( el - changed ))
  run_extras "$1"   # helpers.sh: errs (KEDA warnings on this run), pods and total (each pod's own order count)
  rps=$(( ${ok:-0} / LOAD_SECONDS ))
  REPLICAS_MAX=$maxr; REPLICAS_FINAL=${spec:-0}; SETTLE=$changed; HELD=$held; READY_END=${ready:-0}
  echo "$1: ok ${ok:-0} of ${sent:-0} orders (${rps}/s, failed ${failed:-0}); $pods pods took $total; replicas most $maxr, end ${spec:-0}, held ${held}s; HPA formula max $raw"
  echo "HERO_MEASURE: load_rps[$1]=$rps"
  echo "HERO_MEASURE: replicas_max[$1]=$maxr"
  echo "HERO_MEASURE: replicas_final[$1]=${spec:-0}"
  echo "HERO_MEASURE: seconds_to_settle[$1]=$changed"
  echo "HERO_MEASURE: seconds_held_at_final[$1]=$held"
  echo "HERO_MEASURE: hpa_raw_recommendation_max[$1]=$raw"
  echo "HERO_MEASURE: keda_scaler_errors[$1]=$errs"
  echo "HERO_MEASURE: pods_running_end[$1]=$pods"
  echo "HERO_MEASURE: ready_replicas_end[$1]=${ready:-0}"
  echo "HERO_MEASURE: metric_value_end[$1]=$vend"
  echo "HERO_MEASURE: hpa_desired_max[$1]=$dmax"
  echo "HERO_MEASURE: seconds_to_max[$1]=$tomax"
  [ "${ok:-0}" -gt 0 ] || fail "no order succeeded in $1"
  [ "$total" = "${ok:-0}" ] || echo "  note: the pods counted $total, the load counted ${ok:-0} ok"
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# BEFORE: KEDA 2.21.0 scales the shop StatefulSet on a SignalFlow query of the TOTAL request rate across its pods (the sum),
# with a target of 10 requests a second. Sets up the cluster (the Splunk OTel Collector agent, KEDA, the shop app), then
# runs total-1 and total-2: three pods (what the load needs), 210 s of 30 orders a second, and the replica count recorded every 5 s.
# fix.sh runs the per-pod query (the mean) with everything else the same.
set -uo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
. ./lib.sh
. ./splunk.sh

start_clock 830 not_reproduced

aws eks update-kubeconfig --name "$(terraform output -raw cluster_name)" --region "$AWS_REGION" >/dev/null || fail "could not write kubeconfig"
for v in SPLUNK_REALM SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN SPLUNK_API_TOKEN; do [ -n "${!v:-}" ] || fail "$v is not set"; done

echo "== 1. Waiting for 2 worker nodes"
ready=0
t0=$(date +%s)
while [ $(( $(date +%s) - t0 )) -lt 300 ]; do
  ready=$(kubectl --request-timeout=15s get nodes --no-headers 2>/dev/null | grep -c ' Ready' || true)
  [ "${ready:-0}" -ge 2 ] && break
  sleep 10
done
[ "${ready:-0}" -ge 2 ] || fail "nodes did not become Ready"
kubectl -n kube-system rollout status deploy/coredns --timeout="$(cap 90 600)s" >/dev/null || true
NODE_A=$(kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}')
NODE_B=$(kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[1].metadata.name}')
echo "$NODE_A" > node-a.txt; echo "$NODE_B" > node-b.txt
echo "node A: $NODE_A; node B: $NODE_B"

echo "== 2. One virtualenv with pinned packages on each node (builds run while the charts install)"
sed -e "s/NODE_A/$NODE_A/" -e "s/NODE_B/$NODE_B/" k8s/00-build.yaml | kubectl apply -f - >/dev/null || fail "could not start the builds"

echo "== 3. Splunk OTel Collector chart 0.163.1 and KEDA 2.21.0"
for i in 1 2 3; do
  helm repo add splunk-otel-collector-chart https://signalfx.github.io/splunk-otel-collector-chart >/dev/null 2>&1 &&
    helm repo add kedacore https://kedacore.github.io/charts >/dev/null 2>&1 && helm repo update >/dev/null 2>&1 && break
  sleep 10
done
helm upgrade --install splunk-otel-collector splunk-otel-collector-chart/splunk-otel-collector --version 0.163.1 \
  --namespace splunk --create-namespace --set splunkObservability.realm="$SPLUNK_REALM" \
  --set splunkObservability.accessToken="$SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN" --set clusterName="$LAB_NAME" \
  --set cloudProvider=aws --set distribution=eks >/dev/null || fail "helm could not install the Splunk OTel Collector"
helm upgrade --install keda kedacore/keda --version 2.21.0 --namespace keda --create-namespace >/dev/null || fail "helm could not install KEDA"
kubectl -n splunk rollout status daemonset/splunk-otel-collector-agent --timeout="$(cap 180 560)s" >/dev/null || fail "the agent did not roll out"
for d in keda-operator keda-operator-metrics-apiserver keda-admission-webhooks; do
  kubectl -n keda rollout status "deploy/$d" --timeout="$(cap 180 540)s" >/dev/null || { why_keda; fail "$d did not roll out"; }
done
echo "agent ready on $(kubectl -n splunk get daemonset splunk-otel-collector-agent -o jsonpath='{.status.numberReady}') nodes; $(helm -n keda list -o json | jq -r '.[0] | "\(.chart) (app \(.app_version))"')"
# KEDA reads Splunk with the API token, from a Secret made here from the environment. The token is never printed.
kubectl -n demo create secret generic splunk-keda --from-literal=accessToken="$SPLUNK_API_TOKEN" \
  --from-literal=realm="$SPLUNK_REALM" --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f - >/dev/null || fail "could not create the splunk-keda Secret"

t0=$(date +%s); limit=$(cap 360 500); done_jobs=0
while [ $(( $(date +%s) - t0 )) -lt "$limit" ]; do
  done_jobs=0
  for j in build-a build-b; do
    case "$(kubectl -n demo get job "$j" -o jsonpath='{.status.conditions[?(@.status=="True")].type}' 2>/dev/null)" in
      *Complete*) done_jobs=$(( done_jobs + 1 )) ;;
      *Failed*) kubectl -n demo logs "job/$j" --tail=10; fail "$j failed" ;;
    esac
  done
  [ "$done_jobs" = 2 ] && break
  sleep 10
done
[ "$done_jobs" = 2 ] || fail "the builds did not finish"
kubectl -n demo logs job/build-a --tail=8 2>/dev/null | grep -v '^\[notice\]' | cut -c1-200

echo "== 4. The shop StatefulSet (1 pod, on node A) and its Service"
sed -e "s/LAB_ENV/$LAB_NAME/g" -e "s/NODE_A/$NODE_A/" k8s/10-app.yaml | kubectl apply -f - >/dev/null || fail "could not deploy shop"
kubectl -n demo rollout status statefulset/shop --timeout="$(cap 120 520)s" >/dev/null || { why; fail "shop did not start"; }

echo "== 5. Warm-up: all 8 pods once, so every pod's series exists in Splunk before any run, then KEDA's query is checked"
kubectl -n demo scale statefulset/shop --replicas="$MAX_PODS" >/dev/null || fail "could not scale shop to $MAX_PODS"
kubectl -n demo wait statefulset/shop --for=jsonpath='{.status.readyReplicas}'="$MAX_PODS" --timeout="$(cap 120 470)s" >/dev/null || { why; fail "shop did not reach $MAX_PODS ready pods"; }
kubectl -n demo delete pod load --ignore-not-found --wait=true >/dev/null 2>&1
sed -e "s/NODE_A/$NODE_A/" -e 's/value: "RUN"/value: "total-0"/' -e 's/value: "FIRST"/value: "900001"/' \
    -e 's/value: "LOAD_SECONDS"/value: "20"/' k8s/20-load.yaml | kubectl apply -f - >/dev/null || fail "could not start the warm-up load"
kubectl -n demo wait pod/load --for=jsonpath='{.status.phase}'=Succeeded --timeout=90s >/dev/null || fail "the warm-up load did not finish"
pq=$(query_for total-0); t0=$(date +%s); pv=""
while [ -z "$pv" ] && [ $(( $(date +%s) - t0 )) -lt "$(cap 90 450)" ]; do
  sleep 10; now=$(date +%s); pv=$(sf_last "$pq" "$(( now - 150 ))" "$now")
done
[ -n "$pv" ] || { why_keda; fail "query returned no series: $pq"; }
kq=$(jq -r .total queries.json | sed -e "s/RUN/$LAB_NAME-shop/" -e "s/\.sum()\.mean(over='30s')\.scale(0\.05)\.publish()$/.count().publish()/")
t0=$(date +%s); seen=""
while [ "${seen%.*}" != "$MAX_PODS" ] && [ $(( $(date +%s) - t0 )) -lt "$(cap 180 420)" ]; do
  now=$(date +%s); seen=$(sf_last "$kq" "$(( now - 120 ))" "$now"); [ "${seen%.*}" = "$MAX_PODS" ] || sleep 15
done
echo "warm-up: $seen of $MAX_PODS pods' series in Splunk after $(( $(date +%s) - t0 ))s"
[ "${seen%.*}" = "$MAX_PODS" ] || fail "only ${seen:-0} of $MAX_PODS pods' series reached Splunk in the warm-up"
dims=$(series "sf_metric:http.server.request.duration_count AND run:\"$LAB_NAME-shop\"" | jq -c '[.results[]?.dimensions | {run, pod: .["k8s.pod.name"], method: .["http.request.method"], status: .["http.response.status_code"]}] | unique | .[:3]')
echo "preflight: the total query returned $pv requests a second; series dimensions: $dims"
echo "$dims" | jq -e 'length > 0 and all(.pod != null)' >/dev/null || fail "no series with k8s.pod.name found for the lab label, so the queries can't group by pod"

for run in total-1 total-2; do
  echo "== Run $run: KEDA on the total request rate (the sum across pods), target $TARGET a second, $MAX_PODS pods at most"
  start_run "$run" 90
  [ "$HPA_TYPE" = Value ] && v1=1 || v1=0
  load_run "$run"
  echo "$REPLICAS_MAX $REPLICAS_FINAL $SETTLE $v1 $HELD $READY_END" > "result-$run.txt"
done

echo "== 6. Splunk's view: the cluster and total-1"
wait_cluster "$(cap 60 20)"
echo "Splunk holds $cluster series for k8s.cluster.name $LAB_NAME"
splunk_run total-1

# The before-state: with the total in a Value target, the HPA kept adding pods for a fixed load, up to the maximum.
for run in total-1 total-2; do
  read -r mx fin st v held rdy < "result-$run.txt"
  [ "$v" = 1 ] || fail "$run: KEDA's HPA target isn't type Value"
  [ "$mx" = "$MAX_PODS" ] || fail "$run: the total query reached $mx pods, not the maximum of $MAX_PODS"
done
emit reproduced

# Low-level Splunk Observability Cloud reads used by lib.sh: series and SignalFlow points.
# Sourced, never run alone. Needs SPLUNK_REALM and SPLUNK_API_TOKEN.
API="https://api.${SPLUNK_REALM}.signalfx.com"
STREAM="https://stream.${SPLUNK_REALM}.signalfx.com"
series() { curl -sS --max-time 20 -G -H "X-SF-Token: $SPLUNK_API_TOKEN" "$API/v2/metrictimeseries" --data-urlencode "query=$1" --data-urlencode "limit=1000" 2>/dev/null; }

wait_cluster() {   # seconds. Sets cluster to how many of the cluster's series Splunk holds.
  local t0; t0=$(date +%s); cluster=0
  while [ $(( $(date +%s) - t0 )) -lt "$1" ]; do
    cluster=$(series "k8s.cluster.name:${LAB_NAME}" | jq -r '.count // (.results | length) // 0' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
    [ "${cluster:-0}" -gt 0 ] && break
    sleep 15
  done
}

# SignalFlow answers as a stream of events. This prints one value per point between start and stop, summed across series.
signalflow() {   # program, start ms, stop ms, resolution ms
  curl -sS --max-time 60 -X POST -H "X-SF-Token: $SPLUNK_API_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: text/plain" --data-binary "$1" \
    "$STREAM/v2/signalflow/execute?start=$2&stop=$3&resolution=${4:-10000}&immediate=true" 2>/dev/null |
    awk '/^event:/ { if (b != "") print e "\t" b; e = $2; b = ""; next }
         /^data:/  { sub(/^data: ?/, ""); b = b $0; next }
         END       { if (b != "") print e "\t" b }' |
    jq -Rr --argjson from "$2" --argjson to "$3" 'split("\t") | select(.[0] == "data") | (.[1] | fromjson? // {})
      | select(.logicalTimestampMs >= $from and .logicalTimestampMs < $to) | "\(.logicalTimestampMs) \([.data[]?.value // empty] | add // 0)"' 2>/dev/null
}

# Splunk's view of one run over its own load window (LOAD start and end in load-<run>.txt), read exactly as KEDA reads it:
# the queries.json prefix up to one series per pod, then the total, the mean and the count of those per-pod series, each
# the last point of the load. fix.sh gates the per-pod runs on that count matching the ready replicas.
splunk_run() {   # run label
  local s e kbase
  s=$(sed -n 's/^LOAD start=\([0-9]*\).*/\1/p' "load-$1.txt"); e=$(sed -n 's/^LOAD end=\([0-9]*\).*/\1/p' "load-$1.txt")
  kbase=$(jq -r .total queries.json | sed -e "s/RUN/$LAB_NAME-shop/" -e "s/\.sum()\.mean(over='30s')\.scale(0\.05)\.publish()$//")
  sp_total=$(sf_last "$kbase.sum().scale(0.05).publish()" "$(( e - 40 ))" "$(( e - 6 ))")
  sp_mean=$(sf_last "$kbase.mean().scale(0.05).publish()" "$(( e - 40 ))" "$(( e - 6 ))")
  sp_pods=$(sf_last "$kbase.count().publish()" "$(( e - 40 ))" "$(( e - 6 ))")
  echo "$1 in Splunk, end of load (KEDA's per-pod series): total ${sp_total:-none} orders a second over ${sp_pods:-none} pods, ${sp_mean:-none} a pod"
  SP_PODS=${sp_pods%.*}
  echo "HERO_MEASURE: splunk_pods_reporting[$1]=${SP_PODS:-0}"
  echo "HERO_MEASURE: splunk_mean_end[$1]=${sp_mean:-0}"
}

sf_last() {   # program, start s, stop s: the last non-empty point, one decimal
  local out
  for try in 1 2 3; do
    out=$(signalflow "$1" "$(( $2 * 1000 ))" "$(( $3 * 1000 ))")
    [ -n "$out" ] && break
    sleep 5
  done
  awk 'NF == 2 && $2 != 0 {v = $2} END {if (v != "") printf "%.1f", v}' <<<"$out"
}

# Generic helpers shared by reproduce.sh and fix.sh: the run label, the query for a run, the clock, pods, and each
# run's first order number. Sourced by lib.sh, never run alone.
tag() { echo "$LAB_NAME-$1"; }   # a run's name in output; every run shares the series label $LAB_NAME-shop and is read by its load window

query_for() {   # run label: the run's SignalFlow query from queries.json, with RUN and CLUSTER filled in
  local q; q=$(jq -r --arg k "${1%-*}" '.[$k]' queries.json)
  [ -n "$q" ] && [ "$q" != null ] || fail "queries.json has no query for ${1%-*}"
  q=${q//RUN/$LAB_NAME-shop}; echo "${q//CLUSTER/$LAB_NAME}"
}

start_clock() {   # seconds allowed, the result to print on failure. Every wait is capped so a result always prints.
  START=$(date +%s); LIMIT=$1; FAILED=$2; HERO_DONE=0
  trap '[ "$HERO_DONE" = 1 ] || { HERO_DONE=1; echo "HERO_RESULT: $FAILED"; }' EXIT
}
remaining() { echo $(( START + LIMIT - $(date +%s) )); }
cap() { local want=$1 reserve=$2 r; r=$(( $(remaining) - reserve )); [ "$r" -lt 5 ] && r=5; [ "$want" -lt "$r" ] && echo "$want" || echo "$r"; }
emit() { HERO_DONE=1; echo "HERO_RESULT: $1"; }
fail() { echo "FAIL: $*"; [ "$HERO_DONE" = 1 ] || emit "$FAILED"; exit 0; }

why() { kubectl -n demo get pods -o wide | tail -10; kubectl -n demo get events --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | tail -8 | cut -c1-180; }
why_keda() { kubectl -n keda get pods -o wide | tail -5; kubectl -n keda logs deploy/keda-operator --tail=15 2>&1 | grep -iv token | cut -c1-220; }

first_order() { case "$1" in total-1) echo 1 ;; total-2) echo 100001 ;; perpod-1) echo 200001 ;; perpod-2) echo 300001 ;; esac; }

# KEDA's warnings on this run's ScaledObject (a query window with no data point returns an error and the HPA keeps
# its count), the shop pods by node, and each pod's own count of the orders it took in this run (printed beside the
# load's ok count). Sets errs, pods and total.
run_extras() {   # run label
  local p n
  errs=$(kubectl -n demo get events --field-selector involvedObject.uid=$SO_UID,type=Warning -o json 2>/dev/null |
           jq '[.items[] | (.count // .series.count // 1)] | add // 0')
  kubectl -n demo get events --field-selector involvedObject.uid=$SO_UID,type=Warning \
    -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.reason}: {.message}{"\n"}{end}' 2>/dev/null | sort | uniq -c | head -3 | cut -c1-200 | sed "s/^/  $1 KEDA warning x/"
  echo "  $1 shop pods by node: $(kubectl -n demo get pods -l app=shop -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.spec.nodeName}{"\n"}{end}' | sort | uniq -c | awk '{printf "%s on %s; ", $1, $2}')"
  pods=0; total=0
  for p in $(kubectl -n demo get pods -l app=shop --field-selector=status.phase=Running -o name); do
    n=$(kubectl -n demo exec "$p" -- /lab/venv/bin/python -c 'import json, urllib.request
d = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen("http://localhost:8080/stats", timeout=5)); print(d["blocks"].get("'"$(( $(first_order "$1") / 100000 ))"'", 0))' 2>/dev/null) || continue
    [ "$n" -gt 0 ] && pods=$(( pods + 1 )); total=$(( total + n ))
  done
}

# The live HPA KEDA built for this run carries the behaviour every run shares: a 50 s scale-up window and 1 to 8 pods.
check_hpa() {   # run label
  local w mx mn
  w=$(jq -r '.spec.behavior.scaleUp.stabilizationWindowSeconds' "hpa-$1.json"); mx=$(jq -r '.spec.maxReplicas' "hpa-$1.json")
  mn=$(jq -r '.spec.minReplicas' "hpa-$1.json")
  echo "$1 HPA behaviour: scale-up window ${w}s, replicas ${mn}-${mx}"
  [ "$w" = 50 ] && [ "$mx" = "$MAX_PODS" ] && [ "$mn" = 1 ] || fail "$1: the HPA has window ${w}s and replicas ${mn}-${mx}, not 50 s and 1-$MAX_PODS"
}
